subject: Culture
title: Diwali's Many Origins
description: A fast breakdown of Diwali's Many Origins for builders.

hook.text: Diwali isn't one festival. Hindus, Jains, Sikhs, and some Buddhists each celebrate for different reasons.

buildup.text: Hindus mark Rama's return from exile. Jains honor Mahavira's liberation. Sikhs celebrate Hargobind's release.

discovery.text: The name comes from 'Deepavali'—row of lights. Lamps symbolize knowledge conquering ignorance.

twist.text: Diwali now rivals Christmas in global commerce. India's consumer spending spikes higher than any other holiday.

climax.text: Multiple religions share one festival but tell completely different stories about why they celebrate.

punchline.text: Same lights, different stories behind them.

details.summary: Diwali — the festival of lights — is celebrated by over a billion people, but its origin story varies by religion. Hindus celebrate Rama's return, Sikhs mark Guru Hargobind's release from prison, and Jains honor Mahavira's enlightenment. One festival, multiple meanings, unified by light.
details.whyItMatters: Diwali's multiple origin stories show how festivals can unite diverse communities under shared symbols. Light conquering darkness resonates across religious boundaries.
takeaways: Diwali is celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs, Jains, and some Buddhists
Each religion connects Diwali to a different historical or spiritual event
Oil lamps (diyas) symbolize light's victory over darkness

faq.question: What are the different origin stories of Diwali?
faq.answer: Hindus primarily celebrate Lord Rama's return to Ayodhya after defeating Ravana — citizens lit lamps to guide him home. Sikhs celebrate Guru Hargobind's release from Mughal imprisonment. Jains mark Lord Mahavira's attainment of nirvana. Bengali Hindus worship goddess Kali.

faq.question: How is Diwali celebrated?
faq.answer: Celebrations include lighting oil lamps and candles, setting off fireworks, exchanging sweets and gifts, wearing new clothes, cleaning and decorating homes, and performing puja (worship). Lakshmi, goddess of wealth, is particularly honored.
